units.english: Transport a blind passenger to <planet>
units.italian: Trasporta un passeggero cieco su <planet>

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|description|6200|0
units.english: This blind man, Douglas, wishes to be transported to <destination>, so he can be with his daughter while she undergoes treatment there. He will pay you <payment>.
units.italian: Questo uomo cieco, Douglas, desidera essere trasportato su <destination>, per stare con sua figlia mentre si sottopone a una cura. Ti pagherà <payment>.

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|As you walk through <origin>'s cramped new planetary spaceport, you see a middle-aged man on the other side of the corridor, behind a column of people. He sits on a bench with a suitcase at his side, doing nothing particular aside from the occasional tap of his cane when someone passes by.|6208|0
units.english: As you walk through <origin>'s cramped new planetary spaceport, you see a middle-aged man on the other side of the corridor, behind a column of people. He sits on a bench with a suitcase at his side, doing nothing particular aside from the occasional tap of his cane when someone passes by.
units.italian: Mentre attraversi il nuovo e angusto spazioporto planetario di <origin>, vedi un uomo di mezza età dall'altra parte del corridoio, dietro una colonna di persone. È seduto su una panchina con una valigia al fianco, senza fare nulla di particolare a parte il tocco occasionale del bastone quando qualcuno passa.

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	(Go up to him.)|6210|0
units.english: (Go up to him.)
units.italian: (Avvicinati a lui.)

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	(Ignore him.)|6211|0
units.english: (Ignore him.)
units.italian: (Ignalo.)

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	Wading through the mix of passengers, stevedores, and captains in the overflowing corridor, you reach the man with the cane. It's obvious now that he's blind; he doesn't move to look at you and continues looking straight ahead, but he taps his cane twice when you come by him.|6213|0
units.english: Wading through the mix of passengers, stevedores, and captains in the overflowing corridor, you reach the man with the cane. It's obvious now that he's blind; he doesn't move to look at you and continues looking straight ahead, but he taps his cane twice when you come by him.
units.italian: Facendoti largo fra il misto di passeggeri, stivatori e capitani nel corridoio sovraffollato, raggiungi l'uomo con il bastone. Ora è ovvio che è cieco; non si muove per guardarti e continua a fissare dritto davanti a sé, ma batte il bastone due volte quando gli passi accanto.

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Hello."|6215|0
units.english: "Hello."
units.italian: "Salve."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Are you alright?"|6216|0
units.english: "Are you alright?"
units.italian: "Sta bene?"

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	(Never mind.)|6217|0
units.english: (Never mind.)
units.italian: (Lascia perdere.)

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Yes, hello, how are you doing?" the man responds, shifting his head toward your direction. "I'm here waiting for someone to pick me up," he says in a voice that sounds like he expects it at any moment.|6219|0
units.english: "Yes, hello, how are you doing?" the man responds, shifting his head toward your direction. "I'm here waiting for someone to pick me up," he says in a voice that sounds like he expects it at any moment.
units.italian: "Sì, salve, come sta?" risponde l'uomo, spostando la testa verso di te. "Sono qui in attesa che qualcuno venga a prendermi," dice con una voce che sembra aspettarselo da un momento all'altro.

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Are they far away?"|6223|0
units.english: "Are they far away?"
units.italian: "Sono lontani?"

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Who is it you're looking for?"|6227|0
units.english: "Who is it you're looking for?"
units.italian: "Chi sta cercando?"

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Where is she?"|6232|0
units.english: "Where is she?"
units.italian: "Dov'è lei?"

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"I see. Safe travels to you." (Walk away.)|6236|0
units.english: "I see. Safe travels to you." (Walk away.)
units.italian: "Capisco. Buon viaggio." (Allontanati.)

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Well, I suppose you could say that they are far away, or they could be right here. I don't know." He taps his cane twice more.|6242|0
units.english: "Well, I suppose you could say that they are far away, or they could be right here. I don't know." He taps his cane twice more.
units.italian: "Beh, si potrebbe dire che sono lontani, oppure che potrebbero essere proprio qui. Non lo so." Batte ancora due volte il bastone.

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Someone to take me to my daughter, Anita." Yet again, his cane taps twice.|6248|0
units.english: "Someone to take me to my daughter, Anita." Yet again, his cane taps twice.
units.italian: "Qualcuno che mi porti da mia figlia, Anita." E ancora, il bastone batte due volte.

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	He looks over to his side, as if he feels reserved about something. "She's on <planet>, getting some experimental treatment from the University of New Sydney. I want to be by her side if anything goes wrong, to tell her that I'm there for her, that I love her, and that everything will be okay. She's been waiting for the treatment for so long now. And since nobody else seems to have arrived here yet, I hope you'll be the one to take me there."|6252|0
units.english: He looks over to his side, as if he feels reserved about something. "She's on <planet>, getting some experimental treatment from the University of New Sydney. I want to be by her side if anything goes wrong, to tell her that I'm there for her, that I love her, and that everything will be okay. She's been waiting for the treatment for so long now. And since nobody else seems to have arrived here yet, I hope you'll be the one to take me there."
units.italian: Guarda di lato, come se provasse un certo riserbo. "È su <planet>, si sta sottoponendo a una cura sperimentale all'University of New Sydney. Voglio esserle accanto se qualcosa va storto, dirle che ci sono per lei, che le voglio bene e che andrà tutto bene. Aspetta questa cura da tanto tempo ormai. E visto che nessun altro sembra essere ancora arrivato, spero che sia tu a portarmi là."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Of course, I can take you to <planet>."|6254|0
units.english: "Of course, I can take you to <planet>."
units.italian: "Certo, posso portarla su <planet>."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Sorry, I won't be able to."|6255|0
units.english: "Sorry, I won't be able to."
units.italian: "Spiacente, non potrò."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	The man musters a broad smile, says "Thank you all too much. Would you like to help me with the luggage?" He scans the floor with his cane for it. Later, while boarding, he tells you his name is Douglas Pears, and he promises to you <payment> for transporting him.|6257|0
units.english: The man musters a broad smile, says "Thank you all too much. Would you like to help me with the luggage?" He scans the floor with his cane for it. Later, while boarding, he tells you his name is Douglas Pears, and he promises to you <payment> for transporting him.
units.italian: L'uomo accenna un sorriso largo e dice: "Grazie infinite. Vuole aiutarmi con i bagagli?" Cerca il bagaglio sul pavimento con il bastone. Più tardi, mentre salite a bordo, ti dice che si chiama Douglas Pears e ti promette <payment> per il trasporto.

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Then I will wait until another comes to help me." The blind man taps his cane once more, then returns to looking straight ahead.|6261|0
units.english: "Then I will wait until another comes to help me." The blind man taps his cane once more, then returns to looking straight ahead.
units.italian: "Allora aspetterò che arrivi qualcun altro ad aiutarmi." Il cieco batte ancora una volta il bastone, poi torna a fissare dritto davanti a sé.

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|log|6265|0
units.english: Brought a blind man named Douglas to Chiron so he could visit his daughter, who will undergo experimental treatment at the University of New Sydney.
units.italian: Ho portato un cieco di nome Douglas su Chiron perché potesse far visita a sua figlia, che si sottoporrà a una cura sperimentale all'University of New Sydney.

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|Throughout the trip, Douglas has been relatively quiet and has kept to himself. When you land, he lets you help him bring down his luggage once more; it turns out you needn't have done so because an attendant from the planetary spaceport quickly comes to his side. He guides both of you to the spaceport's intracity transit complex; the bustling spaceport makes it a challenge to keep together, but all of you manage to reach it. From there, you hail a taxi while Douglas arranges for the <payment> to be sent to you.|6268|0
units.english: Throughout the trip, Douglas has been relatively quiet and has kept to himself. When you land, he lets you help him bring down his luggage once more; it turns out you needn't have done so because an attendant from the planetary spaceport quickly comes to his side. He guides both of you to the spaceport's intracity transit complex; the bustling spaceport makes it a challenge to keep together, but all of you manage to reach it. From there, you hail a taxi while Douglas arranges for the <payment> to be sent to you.
units.italian: Durante il viaggio Douglas è stato piuttosto silenzioso e si è tenuto per sé. Quando atterri, ti lascia aiutarlo a scaricare di nuovo i bagagli; si scopre che non ce n'era bisogno, perché un addetto dello spazioporto planetario arriva subito al suo fianco. Vi guida entrambi al complesso dei trasporti urbani dello spazioporto; lo spazioporto affollato rende difficile restare insieme, ma riuscite tutti ad arrivarci. Da lì chiami un taxi mentre Douglas combina l'invio dei <payment>.

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Well, I must go now to the University of New Sydney. They and my daughter are expecting me at their Health Sciences quarter."|6269|0
units.english: "Well, I must go now to the University of New Sydney. They and my daughter are expecting me at their Health Sciences quarter."
units.italian: "Beh, ora devo andare all'University of New Sydney. Loro e mia figlia mi aspettano nel loro quartiere di Scienze della Salute."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Goodbye."|6271|0
units.english: "Goodbye."
units.italian: "Addio."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"I hope your daughter has a safe recovery."|6273|0
units.english: "I hope your daughter has a safe recovery."
units.italian: "Spero che sua figlia si riprenda."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Everything is going to be alright."|6275|0
units.english: "Everything is going to be alright."
units.italian: "Vedrà che andrà tutto bene."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Could I come with you?"|6277|0
units.english: "Could I come with you?"
units.italian: "Potrei venire con lei?"

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Bye, now. I wish you greater luck in your travels and your sights." With that, he taps his cane twice, and then steps into one of New Sydney's taxis, going toward the University of New Sydney campus on the far side of town.|6280|0
units.english: "Bye, now. I wish you greater luck in your travels and your sights." With that, he taps his cane twice, and then steps into one of New Sydney's taxis, going toward the University of New Sydney campus on the far side of town.
units.italian: "Ciao, allora. Ti auguro maggiore fortuna nei tuoi viaggi e nella tua vista." Detto questo, batte due volte il bastone e sale su uno dei taxi di New Sydney, diretto al campus dell'University of New Sydney dall'altra parte della città.

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Yes, thank you so much. I hope so too, of course; actually, it's a little foolish saying that, of course I do. But now I have to go. Again, thank you for making this journey possible."|6284|0
units.english: "Yes, thank you so much. I hope so too, of course; actually, it's a little foolish saying that, of course I do. But now I have to go. Again, thank you for making this journey possible."
units.italian: "Sì, grazie mille. Lo spero anch'io, naturalmente; in realtà è un po' sciocco dirlo, ovvio che lo spero. Ma ora devo andare. Ancora grazie per aver reso possibile questo viaggio."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Goodbye."|6286|0
units.english: "Goodbye."
units.italian: "Addio."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Could I come with you?"|6288|0
units.english: "Could I come with you?"
units.italian: "Potrei venire con lei?"

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|label|6291|0
units.english: come along
units.italian: come along

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	Douglas looks taken aback for a moment, but says, "Well, I suppose you can come along. I'm not sure if the university would let you in, though. But I think Anita would like to meet you, or at least say hello." You get into the taxi with him, and it starts toward New Sydney's University District.|6292|0
units.english: Douglas looks taken aback for a moment, but says, "Well, I suppose you can come along. I'm not sure if the university would let you in, though. But I think Anita would like to meet you, or at least say hello." You get into the taxi with him, and it starts toward New Sydney's University District.
units.italian: Douglas resta sorpreso per un momento, ma dice: "Beh, suppongo che tu possa venire. Non sono sicuro che l'università ti lascerebbe entrare, però. Ma credo che Anita sarebbe contenta di conoscerti, o almeno di salutarti." Sali sul taxi con lui, e parte verso il quartiere universitario di New Sydney.

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"How did you become blind?"|6300|0
units.english: "How did you become blind?"
units.italian: "Come ha perso la vista?"

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"How did becoming blind change your life?"|6305|0
units.english: "How did becoming blind change your life?"
units.italian: "Come le ha cambiato la vita diventare cieco?"

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"How do you feel about the atomic bombings?"|6311|0
units.english: "How do you feel about the atomic bombings?"
units.italian: "Che cosa pensa dei bombardamenti atomici?"

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Was your daughter caught in the atomic bombings?"|6317|0
units.english: "Was your daughter caught in the atomic bombings?"
units.italian: "Sua figlia è stata coinvolta nei bombardamenti atomici?"

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"What happened to your daughter?"|6325|0
units.english: "What happened to your daughter?"
units.italian: "Che cosa è successo a sua figlia?"

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	(Stay silent.)|6331|0
units.english: (Stay silent.)
units.italian: (Resta in silenzio.)

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"It was the fourth of July, 3014. I was in my office, on one of the high rises on the outskirts of the capital, with my office window pointed right at the city center." He turns to look out the window, as if he knew New Sydney's skyline was out there where he couldn't see. In the small lull, he takes an audible breath.|6340|0
units.english: "It was the fourth of July, 3014. I was in my office, on one of the high rises on the outskirts of the capital, with my office window pointed right at the city center." He turns to look out the window, as if he knew New Sydney's skyline was out there where he couldn't see. In the small lull, he takes an audible breath.
units.italian: "Era il quattro luglio 3014. Ero nel mio ufficio, in uno dei grattacieli alla periferia della capitale, con la finestra rivolta dritta verso il centro città." Si volta a guardare fuori dal finestrino, come se sapesse che il profilo di New Sydney è là fuori, dove lui non può vederlo. Nella piccola pausa, fa un respiro udibile.

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"It was a beautiful day that day. I... I remember that Pollux was especially bright and colorful that day, and the songbirds that inhabited the city were alive with sound. They were unusually so. It was very vivid, very strange. Maybe I should have listened to the birds...|6341|0
units.english: "It was a beautiful day that day. I... I remember that Pollux was especially bright and colorful that day, and the songbirds that inhabited the city were alive with sound. They were unusually so. It was very vivid, very strange. Maybe I should have listened to the birds...
units.italian: "Era una bella giornata, quella. Io... ricordo che Pollux era particolarmente luminoso e colorato quel giorno, e gli uccelli canterini che abitavano la città erano pieni di suoni. Insolitamente. Era molto vivido, molto strano. Forse avrei dovuto ascoltare gli uccelli...

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"But when the bomb dropped, I was looking right at it, from my office window. All I could remember next was that I was in a lot of pain, that I couldn't see, but one of my colleagues - thank goodness for her - found me afterwards, during the evacuation, covered in glass from the shockwave. I survived mostly because I was sitting at my terminal and that protected me from the bulk of the shards."|6342|0
units.english: "But when the bomb dropped, I was looking right at it, from my office window. All I could remember next was that I was in a lot of pain, that I couldn't see, but one of my colleagues - thank goodness for her - found me afterwards, during the evacuation, covered in glass from the shockwave. I survived mostly because I was sitting at my terminal and that protected me from the bulk of the shards."
units.italian: "Ma quando la bomba è caduta, la stavo guardando dritta, dalla finestra del mio ufficio. L'unica cosa che ricordo dopo è che avevo molto dolore, che non vedevo più, ma una mia collega, grazie al cielo, mi ha trovato dopo, durante l'evacuazione, coperto di vetri per l'onda d'urto. Sono sopravvissuto soprattutto perché ero seduto al terminale e questo mi ha protetto dalla maggior parte delle schegge."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Hmm... well, it was really only one of many things that hit my life then, not least of which was my newfound blindness, and the loss of my company and my job." He gives a heavy sigh, and he shifts in his seat as if something heavy was placed on his shoulders. "I was able to keep things intact for a while, but no, it was too much. Anything can be taken away from you if you get too used to it."|6349|0
units.english: "Hmm... well, it was really only one of many things that hit my life then, not least of which was my newfound blindness, and the loss of my company and my job." He gives a heavy sigh, and he shifts in his seat as if something heavy was placed on his shoulders. "I was able to keep things intact for a while, but no, it was too much. Anything can be taken away from you if you get too used to it."
units.italian: "Hmm... beh, in realtà è stata solo una delle tante cose che mi hanno colpito la vita, allora, non ultima la nuova cecità, e la perdita della mia azienda e del mio lavoro." Fa un sospiro pesante, e si sposta sul sedile come se qualcosa di pesante gli fosse stato messo sulle spalle. "Sono riuscito a tenere tutto in piedi per un po', ma no, era troppo. Qualsiasi cosa ti può essere tolta se ti ci abitui troppo."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|label|6352|0
units.english: atomic bombings
units.italian: atomic bombings

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"How do I feel about the bombings? Well, they changed everything. In some ways I'm very grateful that it showed - no, it exposed to me, that people, they- there's people that live this way. With no sight. Who need other people to help them just... live. And that there are plenty of people who don't have people to help them live. I was lucky, I could get treatment for my blindness. But others, no...|6356|0
units.english: "How do I feel about the bombings? Well, they changed everything. In some ways I'm very grateful that it showed - no, it exposed to me, that people, they- there's people that live this way. With no sight. Who need other people to help them just... live. And that there are plenty of people who don't have people to help them live. I was lucky, I could get treatment for my blindness. But others, no...
units.italian: "Che cosa provo per i bombardamenti? Beh, hanno cambiato tutto. Per certi versi sono molto grato che mi abbiano mostrato, no, mi abbiano rivelato, che ci sono persone, che- ci sono persone che vivono così. Senza vista. Che hanno bisogno di altri che li aiutino solo a... vivere. E che ci sono un sacco di persone che non hanno nessuno che li aiuti a vivere. Io sono stato fortunato, ho potuto curarmi. Ma altri, no...

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"And for the bombings themselves, they were certainly a malicious act. The Syndicate needs to take full accountability for it, not only for the people who were killed or affected in some form or another. I'm too cynical to say that they will, with all the power they still have in Parliament."|6361|0
units.english: "And for the bombings themselves, they were certainly a malicious act. The Syndicate needs to take full accountability for it, not only for the people who were killed or affected in some form or another. I'm too cynical to say that they will, with all the power they still have in Parliament."
units.italian: "E quanto ai bombardamenti in sé, sono stati certamente un atto malevolo. Il Sindacato deve assumersi piena responsabilità, non solo per le persone uccise o colpite in qualche modo. Sono troppo cinico per dire che lo faranno, con tutto il potere che hanno ancora in Parlamento."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"And for the bombings themselves, they were certainly a malicious act. I hear the authorities are still investigating the bombings, although it's very curious that Korban, the CEO of the Syndicate, resigned as soon as the Republic started poking their heads that way. I'm still not sure who's responsible for the bombings, the deaths, the war... I can only hope the investigation will be thorough."|6365|0
units.english: "And for the bombings themselves, they were certainly a malicious act. I hear the authorities are still investigating the bombings, although it's very curious that Korban, the CEO of the Syndicate, resigned as soon as the Republic started poking their heads that way. I'm still not sure who's responsible for the bombings, the deaths, the war... I can only hope the investigation will be thorough."
units.italian: "E quanto ai bombardamenti in sé, sono stati certamente un atto malevolo. Sento che le autorità stanno ancora indagando, anche se è molto curioso che Korban, l'amministratore delegato del Sindacato, si sia dimesso appena la Repubblica ha cominciato a ficcare il naso da quelle parti. Non sono ancora sicuro di chi sia responsabile dei bombardamenti, delle morti, della guerra... Posso solo sperare che l'indagine sia approfondita."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Luckily, my daughter was off-planet during the bombings. Anita was studying nanoengineering on Vinci and was going to apply for a job at Polymath there. But she gave that up to come take care of me after the bombings. When things were more ironed over, it was the midst of the civil war, and she managed to go back to Vinci and work at Polymath then, but... well, she has not been well since then."|6372|0
units.english: "Luckily, my daughter was off-planet during the bombings. Anita was studying nanoengineering on Vinci and was going to apply for a job at Polymath there. But she gave that up to come take care of me after the bombings. When things were more ironed over, it was the midst of the civil war, and she managed to go back to Vinci and work at Polymath then, but... well, she has not been well since then."
units.italian: "Per fortuna mia figlia era fuori dal pianeta durante i bombardamenti. Anita studiava nanoingegneria su Vinci e stava per candidarsi a un lavoro alla Polymath, là. Ma ha rinunciato per venire a prendersi cura di me dopo i bombardamenti. Quando le cose si sono un po' sistemate, era nel pieno della guerra civile, e riuscì a tornare su Vinci e a lavorare alla Polymath, ma... beh, non sta bene da allora."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"I don't know if I really should tell you this, but Anita was working on a project on nanomachines at Polymath when she got back. She was, uh... infected by them by accident. The experimental treatment is meant to try and eliminate the rogue machines, but since they're so small... that's why the treatment is experimental."|6379|0
units.english: "I don't know if I really should tell you this, but Anita was working on a project on nanomachines at Polymath when she got back. She was, uh... infected by them by accident. The experimental treatment is meant to try and eliminate the rogue machines, but since they're so small... that's why the treatment is experimental."
units.italian: "Non so se dovrei davvero dirtelo, ma Anita stava lavorando a un progetto sulle nanomacchine alla Polymath quando è tornata. È stata, ehm... infettata per caso. La cura sperimentale serve a cercare di eliminare le macchine impazzite, ma visto che sono così piccole... ecco perché la cura è sperimentale."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	Deciding not to ask Douglas anything, you look out the windows of the taxi. You're in the midst of New Sydney, and skyscrapers stare down at your tiny taxi from each side of the avenue, but despite this it is still quite green and cheery, with trees on each side and people walking to work in the morning.|6385|0
units.english: Deciding not to ask Douglas anything, you look out the windows of the taxi. You're in the midst of New Sydney, and skyscrapers stare down at your tiny taxi from each side of the avenue, but despite this it is still quite green and cheery, with trees on each side and people walking to work in the morning.
units.italian: Decidendo di non chiedere nulla a Douglas, guardi fuori dai finestrini del taxi. Siete nel mezzo di New Sydney, e i grattacieli guardano dall'alto il tuo piccolo taxi da entrambi i lati del viale, ma nonostante questo è ancora piuttosto verde e allegro, con alberi su entrambi i lati e gente che va a piedi al lavoro la mattina.

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	As the taxi drives on a highway on the edge of a small hill, the window gives you a panorama of the suburbs of New Sydney and the two skylines on each side, one marking the commercial sector where the spaceport is prominent in its gleaming steel-glass architecture, and the other being the University District, a series of clean and white, flowing buildings and skyscrapers. Far away on the horizon, you can barely notice the smokestacks of factories.|6390|0
units.english: As the taxi drives on a highway on the edge of a small hill, the window gives you a panorama of the suburbs of New Sydney and the two skylines on each side, one marking the commercial sector where the spaceport is prominent in its gleaming steel-glass architecture, and the other being the University District, a series of clean and white, flowing buildings and skyscrapers. Far away on the horizon, you can barely notice the smokestacks of factories.
units.italian: Mentre il taxi percorre un'autostrada sul bordo di una piccola collina, il finestrino ti offre un panorama dei sobborghi di New Sydney e dei due profili di skyline ai lati: uno segna il settore commerciale, dove lo spazioporto spicca con la sua architettura lucida d'acciaio e vetro, e l'altro è il quartiere universitario, una serie di edifici e grattacieli candidi e dalle linee fluide. Lontano all'orizzonte si distinguono a malapena le ciminiere delle fabbriche.

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	The taxi enters the University district proper now, and the window shows thongs of energetic university students from the University of New Sydney travelling to and from lectures and classrooms; going over steel walkways that run from building to building above you, and on footpaths beside the streets; clutching their backpacks and data pads. Your datapad shows that University isn't actually the only university district in New Sydney. The University of Chiron's campus is on the other side of town, presumably to keep the fierce competition between the two institutions from boiling over each other.|6395|0
units.english: The taxi enters the University district proper now, and the window shows thongs of energetic university students from the University of New Sydney travelling to and from lectures and classrooms; going over steel walkways that run from building to building above you, and on footpaths beside the streets; clutching their backpacks and data pads. Your datapad shows that University isn't actually the only university district in New Sydney. The University of Chiron's campus is on the other side of town, presumably to keep the fierce competition between the two institutions from boiling over each other.
units.italian: Il taxi entra ora nel quartiere universitario vero e proprio, e il finestrino mostra fiumi di studenti pieni di energia dell'University of New Sydney che vanno e vengono dalle lezioni e dalle aule; attraversano passerelle d'acciaio che corrono da un edificio all'altro sopra di voi, e marciapiedi lungo le strade, stringendo zaini e tavolette dati. La tua tavoletta mostra che quella non è in realtà l'unica zona universitaria di New Sydney. Il campus dell'University of Chiron è dall'altra parte della città, presumibilmente per evitare che la feroce competizione fra i due istituti tracimi.

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	Eventually, the taxi passes by a sign for the "UNS Health Sciences" quarter, which by the looks of it takes up an entire section of the University District. The taxi pulls up beside the entrance of the university hospital, where you help Douglas out with his luggage. The building is stark from the outside, to match the architecture of the surroundings, yet strangely colorful on the inside, as if the person building it decided that hospital interiors were far too unimaginative.|6401|0
units.english: Eventually, the taxi passes by a sign for the "UNS Health Sciences" quarter, which by the looks of it takes up an entire section of the University District. The taxi pulls up beside the entrance of the university hospital, where you help Douglas out with his luggage. The building is stark from the outside, to match the architecture of the surroundings, yet strangely colorful on the inside, as if the person building it decided that hospital interiors were far too unimaginative.
units.italian: Alla fine il taxi passa davanti a un'insegna del quartiere "UNS Health Sciences", che a quanto pare occupa un'intera sezione del quartiere universitario. Il taxi si ferma accanto all'ingresso dell'ospedale universitario, dove aiuti Douglas a scendere con i bagagli. L'edificio è spoglio dall'esterno, per adeguarsi all'architettura circostante, eppure stranamente colorato all'interno, come se chi l'ha costruito avesse deciso che gli interni degli ospedali erano fin troppo privi di fantasia.

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	After a short queue, you reach the reception with Douglas. The receptionist, placed behind a sterile-looking screen that looks far out of place with the colorful hallways, asks with a well-practiced smile, "How may I help you?"|6402|0
units.english: After a short queue, you reach the reception with Douglas. The receptionist, placed behind a sterile-looking screen that looks far out of place with the colorful hallways, asks with a well-practiced smile, "How may I help you?"
units.italian: Dopo una breve coda, arrivi alla reception con Douglas. L'addetta, dietro uno schermo dall'aria sterile che stona molto con i corridoi colorati, chiede con un sorriso ben collaudato: "Come posso aiutarvi?"

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"We're looking for Anita Pears. Where can we find her?"|6404|0
units.english: "We're looking for Anita Pears. Where can we find her?"
units.italian: "Stiamo cercando Anita Pears. Dove possiamo trovarla?"

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	For a moment, the receptionist shuffles information around on her terminal. "Is one of you a parent?"|6405|0
units.english: For a moment, the receptionist shuffles information around on her terminal. "Is one of you a parent?"
units.italian: Per un momento l'addetta sfoglia informazioni sul terminale. "Uno di voi è un genitore?"

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"I'm the father, Douglas Pears," he replies.|6406|0
units.english: "I'm the father, Douglas Pears," he replies.
units.italian: "Sono il padre, Douglas Pears," risponde lui.

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	She takes a few more seconds before looking at you and saying, "Ah, but we cannot let you in. Only Mr. Pears is booked in for his daughter's procedure; we have a family-only policy, to keep the privacy of our patients."|6407|0
units.english: She takes a few more seconds before looking at you and saying, "Ah, but we cannot let you in. Only Mr. Pears is booked in for his daughter's procedure; we have a family-only policy, to keep the privacy of our patients."
units.italian: Le serve qualche altro secondo prima di guardarti e dire: "Ah, ma non possiamo farla entrare. Solo il signor Pears ha l'autorizzazione per la procedura di sua figlia; abbiamo una regola che ammette solo i familiari, per tutelare la privacy dei nostri pazienti."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Alright."|6409|0
units.english: "Alright."
units.italian: "D'accordo."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Are you sure?"|6411|0
units.english: "Are you sure?"
units.italian: "Ne è sicura?"

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"We can't allow immediate exceptions, sorry. There's nothing I can do."|6412|0
units.english: "We can't allow immediate exceptions, sorry. There's nothing I can do."
units.italian: "Non possiamo concedere eccezioni immediate, mi dispiace. Non posso fare nulla."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	Douglas gives you a compassionate look, and says to the receptionist, "There'll be no worry." He turns back to you once more and says, "I'm sure that when Anita is recovered and well, we can meet again some day. I don't want to keep you from your business too long, either. I expect ship captains are busy folk." He comes up to you and, to your surprise, gives you a hug. "Thank you so much for bringing me here and coming along with me. I really can't say how I want to express my gratitude. But I hope we meet again. Farewell."|6414|0
units.english: Douglas gives you a compassionate look, and says to the receptionist, "There'll be no worry." He turns back to you once more and says, "I'm sure that when Anita is recovered and well, we can meet again some day. I don't want to keep you from your business too long, either. I expect ship captains are busy folk." He comes up to you and, to your surprise, gives you a hug. "Thank you so much for bringing me here and coming along with me. I really can't say how I want to express my gratitude. But I hope we meet again. Farewell."
units.italian: Douglas ti lancia uno sguardo compassionevole e dice all'addetta: "Non c'è problema." Si volta di nuovo verso di te e dice: "Sono certo che, quando Anita sarà guarita e starà bene, potremo rivederci un giorno. E non voglio trattenerti troppo dai tuoi affari. Immagino che i capitani di nave siano gente indaffarata." Ti viene incontro e, con tua sorpresa, ti abbraccia. "Grazie mille per avermi portato qui e per essere venuto con me. Non so davvero come esprimere la mia gratitudine. Ma spero che ci rivedremo. Addio."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Goodbye."|6416|0
units.english: "Goodbye."
units.italian: "Addio."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	"Farewell to you too."|6417|0
units.english: "Farewell to you too."
units.italian: "Addio anche a lei."

units.id: mission:Blind Man from Martini|	With that, he grabs his cane and his luggage, and follows a hospital attendant toward his daughter's room, leaving you in the reception.|6428|0
units.english: With that, he grabs his cane and his luggage, and follows a hospital attendant toward his daughter's room, leaving you in the reception.
units.italian: Detto questo, prende il bastone e i bagagli, e segue un addetto dell'ospedale verso la stanza di sua figlia, lasciandoti alla reception.
